module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Chvátal's Conjecture

*References:*

* [A Conjecture in Extremal Combinatorics](https://users.encs.concordia.ca/~chvatal/conjecture.html)
* [Chvátal's Conjecture and Correlation Inequalities](https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.08954)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Chvatal

variable {α : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]

/-- A family F of sets is Decreasing if it is closed under taking subsets. -/
def Decreasing (F : Finset (Finset α)) : Prop :=
    ∀ A B : Finset α, B ⊆ A → A ∈ F → B ∈ F

/-- A family F of sets is Intersecting if each pair of members has nonempty intersection. -/
def Intersecting (F : Finset (Finset α)) : Prop :=
    ∀ A ∈ F, ∀ B ∈ F, A ∩ B ≠ ∅

/--
If F is a decreasing family of sets of some finite type α, then there is some element
x of α such that the family consisting of all members of F containing x is an intersecting
subfamily of F with maximal cardinality.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem exists_maximal_star :
    ∀ F : Finset (Finset α), Decreasing F →
        ∃ x : α, ∀ G, G ⊆ F → Intersecting G → G.card ≤ { A ∈ F | x ∈ A }.card := by
  sorry

reformulations.difference: Chvátal's webpage counts {∅} as intersecting and explicitly excludes the independence system F = {∅}. Lean instead requires nonempty intersections even when A = B, and does not exclude F = {∅}. This follows the intersecting-family convention in the cited arXiv paper.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The two intersecting predicates differ exactly at the family {∅}. For F ≠ {∅}, this extra competitor cannot change the maximum: if {∅} ⊆ F, then F contains a nonempty A, and the Lean-intersecting singleton family {A} already has the same cardinality, 1. For F = {∅}, Lean's only intersecting subfamily is empty, and every star is empty, so the additional case holds automatically because α is nonempty. A Lean proof establishes the equivalence of the complete conjectures in /workspace/review/scratch.lean (ChvatalReview.full_web_equivalence), without using the conjecture theorem or sorry.

sources_consulted: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1608.08954 — Friedgut, Kahn, Kalai and Keller, Chvátal's Conjecture and Correlation Inequalities, §1 definitions and Conjecture 1.1; §2.1, Proposition 2.1.
Mathlib/Combinatorics/SetFamily/Intersecting.lean; Mathlib/Data/Finset/{Defs,Filter,Card,Lattice/Basic}.lean; Mathlib/Order/Defs/Unbundled.lean, in the checked-out Mathlib dependency.
review.notes: Checked all three declarations. Decreasing expresses subset closure, and Intersecting matches the arXiv definition. The quantifier order chooses one point for each F that works for every intersecting subfamily. Proved that the filtered star is automatically an intersecting subfamily, so the cardinality bound expresses a genuine maximum. #print confirmed the theorem retains Fintype and Nonempty assumptions. Scratch tests covered empty families, {∅}, singleton ground sets, and all families on ground sets of sizes 1–3; equivalence proofs have no sorryAx dependency. Both cited sources present the general conjecture as open.
